side_a: CC 3.3.13 each chunk is one fMP4 segment (`moof` + `mdat`), independently hashable, ordered by sequence number; `codec` is stream-level, once
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.1 makes the realtime chunk payload codec **application-defined and opaque to the substrate**
note: 3.3.13 fixes a live_stream chunk as an fMP4 segment whose concatenation after the init segment is a valid video/mp4. 5.3.3.2.x make a call's stream a live_stream whose chunks are per-layer codec units tagged by codec_id and ChunkLayer, at most 252 bytes of plaintext on a base link (5.3.3.2.3), "the same sealed object" live and stored (5.3.3.2). A receiver built to one cannot decode the other, and the recording rule (init then chunks is the file) does not hold for layered chunks.

side_a: CC 3.4.1: Revocation rides the tombstone, `withdraws`/`recants`, supersession, or the halt latch, and nothing else.
side_b: CC 3.2: It is never revoked by a halt, which reaches an agent's act gate and no root

side_a: CC 2.6.7 Consumers receiving an attestation whose `asserted_at` is more than 5 minutes in the future MUST reject it as malformed.
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1 So a sealed row signed months earlier is live when published, and a future-dated one cannot buy a longer pause.
note: Sibling of C036 (what holds past valid_until, open with the steward), on the other signed instant. CC 4.2.1 ('The signer-chosen `asserted_at` plays no part') and CC 2.4 (the kill switch depends on no gate 'beyond verifying those bytes and the holder roster') admit a halt whatever its asserted_at; CC 2.6.7 states no exception and refuses a future-dated one. One reader's node latches, the other's refuses the row. The family model's freshness cell for accord:invoke:constitutional is the generic one (future skew at most 5 min), so the data follows CC 2.6.7.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.1: "anyone who joins (open admission); replicated to the roster's nodes"
side_b: CC 3.2: "a non-member reads the listing and may read the content by asking a member's node"
note: Who reads a public room's content. The readers cell of the CC 4.4.3.2.1 tier table gives it to those who join; CC 3.2 and the CC 5.2 table give it to any non-member who asks a member's node, without joining. CC 5.2's lead ('served to a node in its audience and to no other') reads with CC 4.4.3.2.1, its own table row with CC 3.2. A node built from the tier table refuses a non-member's read; one built from CC 3.2 serves it. C292 settled the crypto-tier pair, not this one. CC 3.2 is the home of the public room.

side_a: CC 2.1: "A change is a charter re-scrub, witnessed by the directory before it."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json trust:{job}:{version}: supersede roles author, policy selfAct, guard []; the charter guard sits on authorize only
note: A charter re-scrub that changes the witness directory must be witnessed by the directory before it (CC 2.1, CC 3.2 T6) and may list only a key with a live lineage_witness acceptance. side_a: CC 3.2 The founder's standing **`membership:proposal:v1`** is then addressed to any requester
side_b: CC 3.1.3.2 `expires_at` is REQUIRED on a proposal, after its `asserted_at` and at most 30 days later.
note: An open room's proposal is called standing in CC 3.2, 3.1.3 and the 4.4.3.2.3 pseudo-code, with no word on expiry; CC 3.1.3.2 and constants.tsv (membership_proposal_max_secs) cap every proposal at 30 days and make an acceptance of an expired one terminal (membership_proposal_expired). side_a: CC 7.3.3 That is the one trigger: the criteria of Annex D ([CC 8.8.3](part_8_appendices.md#8.8.3)) are what the evaluation then applies, and the Stewardship Tier never triggers it.

note: Annex I opens a Catastrophic-Risk Evaluation by Stewardship Tier: a deployment at ST 3 with RM 3 (CIS 7 × RM 3 = 21) is evaluated under Annex I and never under CC 7.3.3. side_a: CC 3.2 "the head de-witnessed (its counted witnesses revoked before their `signed_at`, or the directory collapsed to non-independent keys)"
side_b: CC 3.2 "A consumer that holds a witnessed head MUST refuse a competing head that is not witnessed"
note: T8 lists a directory collapse among the NotRooted cases and as a transition (a new witnessed head that removes a leg -> NotRooted). T6 judges independence at the cosignature's signed_at ('a later change of role neither voids an earlier cosignature'), verifies a head against its parent's directory, and has the holder refuse an unwitnessed head; T4/T4a say nothing but a revocation detaches an attached node. One reader detaches every attached node at the collapse; the other keeps them Rooted on the last witnessed head. T4 and the nearest-verifying-ancestor input support the second. Confidence medium.

side_a: CC 3.2: "On the base it is the cosigned `group:roster:v1` row, whose cosigners are the version's signers"
side_b: CC 4.2.6: "The proposal and the participation each sign a distinct, wire-isolated canonical-bytes domain"
note: Text against text. CC 3.2 and the CC 3.1.3 group:roster row make an accord roster version a cosigned row: additional_scrubs over the record's own canonical bytes, reaching the roster-change threshold. CC 4.2.6 has each holder sign an accord_participation preimage (a vote over the proposer's nonce) and says the decision bundle signs nothing. A verifier built from one refuses the roster change the other produces; no sentence says how participations become the version's cosignatures. C051 notes only that the objects are missing from the CC 4.2.1 enumeration.
